newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bills repo rates end up, spot down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bills repo rates end up, spot down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed slightly up on Thursday due to a rise in the Shanghai A share market today, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract rose to 10 percent from 9.48 percent on Wednesday.
Turnover rose to 12.88 million lots from 5.53 million on Wednesday. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said the rise of the Shanghai domestic A share market was the major factor pushing up early-maturing contracts.
Another reason for the rise was the listing of three education funds on Friday, traders added.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down, led by a poor performance of the seven-year bond listed a week ago, trader said.
The most active ten-year bond that matures in 2006 closed down to 115.8 yuan from 117.44 yuan on Wednesday.
Combined volume of the nine-contract market rose to 2.80 million lots from 1.21 million on Wednesday.
"Technical charts indicated that the most active bond will fall to the 114-yuan support level in the short term," a local analyst said.
